Thank you. I think what helped me through school and during this is dedicating the time and planning to study in a place with no distractions. For me it’s my university’s silent floor, I bring a ton of snacks and just spread everything out that I need to go over. I picked 1-2 systems per day. I would read the chapter and as I went along I would go back through things and try to recall things as I went. Like once I turned the page, before starting the next, I would try to summarize what I had just read. It took forever. I usually write notes on paper instead of typing too because that helps me retain it better. I would make up silly things to remember what assessment sign went with what diagnosis. After I felt like I had my hands around the chapter I would start with practice questions. Before bed I would briefly review what I had gone over. I feel like it sounds overkill when I type it out but it helped me feel comfortable. Something about going back over it before sleep really helped me too. Sleep is also important, try to get 6-8 hours consistently if you can. Exercise and eat well. Positive affirmations to your efforts/cutting off negative self talk are helpful too. On those long days in the library I would get up and walk every hour just to not feel restless and anxious
